subject: psychology
title: Schizophrenia Explained: Symptoms & Diagnosis
welcome_lead: Positive and negative symptoms — and why diagnosis is hard.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology schizophrenia symptoms positive negative diagnosis DSM ICD.
final_note: Schizophrenia is plural — a cluster, not a single disease.

concepts.def: Sensory experience without external stimulus — often auditory.
Loss of motivation — a negative symptom.
Poverty of speech — reduced verbal fluency.
Crow 1980 — Type I positive, Type II negative.

walkthroughs.body_html: Positive symptoms add experiences: hallucinations (auditory in 70% of cases — Slade & Bentall 1988), delusions (Sartorius 1986: persecutory most common). Negative symptoms remove function: avolition, alogia, flat affect, anhedonia.

DSM-5 requires one positive symptom from hallucination, delusion or disorganised speech for one month plus disturbance for 6 months. ICD-11 requires two symptoms for one month. Inter-rater reliability is moderate (kappa = 0.46 in Cheniaux 2009).

Crow (1980) distinguished Type I (positive symptoms, acute onset, good response to antipsychotics, no structural brain change) from Type II (negative symptoms, chronic, poor response, ventricular enlargement). The two-syndrome model captures heterogeneity.
